newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia June trade deficit.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia June trade deficit.

text.p: Malaysia reported a 2.8 billion ringgit monthly trade deficit for June on Monday against a surplus of 156.2 million ringgit in May. Following are comments from analysts and economists.
KEVIN CHEW, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CASPIAN SECURITIES
"On the surface, it's quite a huge figure and above market expectations. It was very much inflated by imports of bulky items again.
"At the moment, exports were also not doing that well. The key thing to watch is whether exports will improve in the second half of the year.
"Those who were expecting an improvement in the current account deficit this year will probably have to revise their numbers."
P.K. BASU, REGIONAL ECONOMIST AT UBS SECURITIES IN SINGAPORE
"I am absolutely certain it has to include quite a few aircraft.

One encouraging thing is that exports are up year on year. Semicondctors declined year-on-year for the first six months, but the big swing factor has been transportation equipment. The sheer size of June's equipment imports boggles the mind.
Malaysia imported quite a few ships and planes in the month of June itself. Malaysia can achieve its target (for 1997) so long as we don't have too many imports of aircraft and ships this year."
KOSTAS PANAGIOTOU, SENIOR ECONOMIST AT KIM ENG SECURITIES,
"The figure was shocking. Exports were very flat but imports have been very, very strong.
"I think a lot of people will be revising both their trade and current account projections for the year.
"It doesn't look encouraging at all. The fact that exports are still not picking up is very worrying.
"The stock market was already talking about a large deficit today. Confirmation of it will trigger further downside in the market tomorrow."
